messages.subject: colors in a stacked bar
parts:
Lets day we have a dataframe aa: 
  groep variable     value
1     a   Hotten 0.6385186
2     b   Hotten 4.0225252
3     c   Hotten 1.3853093
4     d   Hotten 3.5253940
5     a      Tot 0.9440719
6     b      Tot 0.1308397
7     c      Tot 0.3958619
8     d      Tot 0.1689032
(this dataframe is the result of melting).
Now i can make a stacked bar chart using 

ggplot(aa)+aes(x=groep,y=value,fill=variable)+geom_bar(stat='identity')

But is it possible to specify the colors of the stacked bar? Now the colors of the stacked variables are blue and something like red. How can i specify this color (normally this is done with fill, but now fill is used to specify the grouped variable).
Thanks
Frans

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Re: colors in a stacked bar
parts:
Hey Frans,
I think you are looking for scale_fill_manual in this case.

## Note, it is generally good style to provide small sample data in R code. 
## There are many locations to find guides on minimal reproducible examples, e.g.,
## http://stackoverflow.com/questions/5963269/how-to-make-a-great-r-reproducible-example
aa <- data.frame( groep = rep(letters[1:4], 2), variable = c(rep("Hotten", 4), rep("Tot", 4)), value = rnorm(8)+5)
## Use grey (via hex) and blue (via text)
p <- ggplot(aa)+aes(x=groep,y=value,fill=variable)+geom_bar(stat='identity') + scale_fill_manual(values = c("#CCCCCC", "blue"))
## I personally like the stacking to match the legend, so I always reverse the legend
p <- p + guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE))

Best wishes,
Doug
